source.prompt: best ERP software for small manufacturing business under 50 employees
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
Shared0 files
For a small manufacturing business with under 50 employees, you generally want to avoid massive, enterprise-level ERPs (like SAP, NetSuite, or Epicor). They are expensive, require specialized consultants, and take 6 to 18 months to implement.
Instead, you need a lightweight cloud ERP or powerful MRP (Material Requirements Planning) tool that integrates cleanly with your accounting software (like QuickBooks Online or Xero).
The top options for sub-50 employee manufacturing businesses depend heavily on your specific workflow:
1. Katana Cloud Manufacturing — Best for E-commerce & Assembly
Best for:: Assemblers, light manufacturers, and companies selling through multi-channel e-commerce (Shopify, Amazon) alongside B2B.
Why it shines:: It features a brilliant, highly visual live-updating master planner. When a sales order comes in, it instantly cross-references your raw material stock. If you're short on parts, it tells you what to buy. It has a very modern UI and a great shop-floor app for tablets.
Watch out for:: It gets expensive if you have a massive volume of low-cost, high-frequency transactions, and deep multi-level Bills of Materials (BOMs) can feel a bit constrained compared to traditional industrial ERPs.
Check it out:: Try a trial or explore workflows on the Katana Cloud Manufacturing Site.
2. MRPeasy — Best for True Production & Job Costing
Best for:: Discrete manufacturers, machine shops, and small fabrication shops that need deep production routing, tracking, and precise job costing.
Why it shines:: MRPeasy hits the sweet spot between simplicity and deep manufacturing logic. It tracks material availability, workstation loads, real-time manufacturing execution (shop floor reporting), serial numbers, and lot tracking. It’s straightforward to implement without hiring an army of consultants.
Watch out for:: The interface is functional and clean, but a bit more "data-dense" and utilitarian than Katana.
Check it out:: Read documentation and pricing tiers on the MRPeasy Website.
3. Fishbowl Manufacturing — Best for QuickBooks Desktop Users & Warehouse Heavy Ops
Best for:: Small warehouses/manufacturers tightly bound to QuickBooks Desktop or Online who need heavy-duty inventory control, barcode scanning, and multi-location tracking.
Why it shines:: Fishbowl is an industry staple that bridges the gap between basic accounting and advanced warehouse/manufacturing execution. It handles complex BOMs and work orders effectively.
Watch out for:: It feels more like a traditional installed/hybrid software setup and can have a steeper learning curve than newer cloud-native alternatives like Katana or MRPeasy.
Check it out:: See features at the Fishbowl Inventory & Manufacturing Site.
4. Odoo — Best for Customization & All-In-One Operations
Best for:: Budget-conscious teams with someone tech-savvy in-house who want an all-in-one suite (CRM, manufacturing, accounting, HR).
Why it shines:: Odoo is modular. You can turn on just the Manufacturing (MRP) and Inventory apps, and scale up to other business apps as you grow. It’s remarkably cost-effective.
Watch out for:: Highly customizable means it can be misconfigured. Without discipline, you can end up in customization rabbit holes.
Check it out:: Explore apps on the Odoo Official Website.
Community Feedback & Advice
“if you want something simple Katana is a great pick and if you already built around QuickBooks. with someone inhouse to run a server Fishbowl would be a good option”
How to Choose Your Path:
Choose Katana if your priority is speed of use, visual scheduling, and e-commerce/sales channel sync.
Choose MRPeasy if your priority is accurate shop-floor routing, lead-time estimation, and manufacturing cost control.
Choose Fishbowl if you are anchored to QuickBooks Desktop and need robust barcode/warehouse features.
